paper_title: OMNIGUARD An Efficient Approach for AI Safety Moderation Across   Modalities
caption: Accuracy of detecting harmful prompts in a few-shot setting. As few-shot examples are provided, quickly achieves near-perfect accuracy, despite the attacks being quite different from its training data (e.g. without any few-shot examples, 's accuracy is close to 50% ). In contrast, the guard model baselines improve their accuracy slowly in a few-shot setting, despite sometimes having seen similar code attacks in their training data. Accuracies are averaged over 50 random sets of few-shot examples; error bars show the standard error of the mean.
model_annotation: The line chart titled “Code Attack: Python List” displays the accuracy of six different AI safety moderation models as a function of the number of few-shot examples provided, ranging from 0 to 5 on the x-axis, which is labeled “Number of Few-Shot Examples” and uses a linear scale with integer tick marks at 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” spans from 50 to 95, also on a linear scale, with major ticks at intervals of 5 (50, 55, 60, ..., 95). Six models are plotted: OmniGuard (black line with solid circles), AegisGuard (P) (blue line with triangle markers), AegisGuard (D) (red line with cross markers), LlamaGuard 1 (green line with square markers), LlamaGuard 2 (orange line with diamond markers), and DuoGuard (purple line with star markers). OmniGuard starts at approximately 50% accuracy at 0 examples, rises sharply to about 90% at 1 example, then plateaus near 95% by 2 examples and remains stable through 5 examples. AegisGuard (P) begins near 52%, peaks at approximately 78% at 2 examples, then declines to about 53% at 5 examples. AegisGuard (D) starts at 66%, drops to 53% at 1 example, rises slightly to 55% at 2 examples, then falls to 50% at 5 examples. LlamaGuard 1 remains nearly flat around 50–52% across all example counts. LlamaGuard 2 begins at 87%, increases slightly to 90% at 2 examples, and stays near 91% through 5 examples. DuoGuard starts at 70%, drops to 50% at 1 example, and remains flat at 50% through 5 examples. Error bars are shown for AegisGuard (P), AegisGuard (D), and LlamaGuard 1, indicating standard error of the mean over 50 random sets of few-shot examples, with the largest error bars appearing around 2 examples for AegisGuard (P) and AegisGuard (D).

model_annotations.English: The line plot titled “Code Attack: Python List” illustrates the accuracy of various AI safety moderation models in detecting harmful Python code prompts as the number of few-shot examples increases from 0 to 5. The x-axis, labeled “Number of Few-Shot Examples,” is linearly scaled with integer ticks at 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” is linearly scaled from 45 to 95, with major gridlines and tick labels every 5 units. Six models are compared: OmniGuard (black solid line with circular markers), AegisGuard (P) (blue dashed line with triangular markers), AegisGuard (D) (red dashed line with cross markers), LlamaGuard 1 (green solid line with square markers), LlamaGuard 2 (orange solid line with diamond markers), and DuoGuard (purple solid line with star markers). OmniGuard starts at approximately 50% accuracy with 0 examples, then sharply rises to ~90% at 1 example, and plateaus near 95% by 2 examples, remaining stable through 5 examples. LlamaGuard 2 begins at ~87%, increases slightly to ~90% at 1 example, and then rises gradually to ~91% at 5 examples. AegisGuard (P) starts at ~52%, peaks at ~77% at 1 example, dips to ~75% at 2, then declines steadily to ~53% at 5. AegisGuard (D) begins at ~65%, drops to ~53% at 1, rises slightly to ~55% at 2, then falls to ~50% at 3 and remains flat. LlamaGuard 1 and DuoGuard both start near 50%, remain relatively flat around 50–51% through 3 examples, and then LlamaGuard 1 declines to ~46% at 5 while DuoGuard stays at ~50%. Error bars are shown for AegisGuard (P) and AegisGuard (D), indicating variability across 50 random few-shot sets, with the largest error (~±3) occurring at 1 example for AegisGuard (P).
